inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: In the midst of escalating tensions in the Middle East driven by deep-rooted power imbalances and historical inequalities, the US has proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan routed to Iran through Pakistan. Iran has pushed back strongly with five counter-conditions that correctly insist on halting the aggression, securing fair compensation for the inflicted harms, and affirming their sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. This stands as a clear challenge to the structural inequalities where dominant players like the US and Israel prioritize maintaining control over addressing the systemic roots of these conflicts. As expected, Israel remains doubtful of any real Iranian acceptance and is escalating its assertions of pre-emptive strike rights, which only deepens the cycle of domination and endangers the security of vulnerable populations caught in between. Real progress will require institutional reform to dismantle these imbalances, rather than talks that just cover for ongoing aggression.
